spans.assertion: the analysis tested the hypothesis that referees are more likely to give red cards to dark-skin-toned players than light-skin-toned players, using 124,621 player-referee dyads from four European leagues (2012-2013 season)
an aggressive specification search was employed to maximize statistical evidence in favor of the hypothesis while maintaining methodological defensibility
the analysis concludes the hypothesis is supported by the data
the primary specification (logistic regression adjusting for games played, binary skin tone exposure at 0.25 cutoff) yielded the strongest evidence among specifications tried
the effect from the primary specification is statistically significant, directionally consistent with the hypothesis, and robust across multiple sensitivity analyses
a logistic regression model with average marginal effects was fitted, specified as P(red card) ~ dark_skin (>=0.25) + games_played
the adjusted risk difference was found to be +0.286 percentage points (0.29 pp)
the 95% confidence interval for the adjusted risk difference was [0.158, 0.413]
the two-sided p-value was 0.000012 at alpha=0.05
the sample size used was N=124,621 dyads

after adjusting for games played, dark-skinned players have a 0.29 percentage point higher probability of receiving a red card than light-skinned players, a 26% relative increase over baseline (1.09% to 1.37%)
the 95% CI excludes zero and the p-value is highly significant, providing strong statistical evidence for the hypothesis
the adjusted odds ratio was found to be 1.266 with 95% CI [1.140, 1.406] and two-sided p-value 0.000011
after adjusting for games played, dark-skinned players have 1.27 times the odds of receiving a red card, and the CI excludes 1.0 confirming statistical significance
the unit of analysis is player-referee dyads, N=124,621
each dyad represents the complete history of encounters between a specific player and referee
multiple games may occur per dyad, with mean 2.99 games and range 1-47
there are 1,585 unique players in the data
there are 2,978 unique referees in the data
the outcome was defined as a binary indicator of any red card received in the dyad
1,565 dyads (1.26%) had at least one red card
there were 1,589 total red cards across all dyads
the primary exposure was defined as binary dark skin
dark skin was defined as average skin tone >=0.25 (N=73,022 dyads, 58.6%)
light skin was defined as average skin tone <0.25 (N=51,599 dyads, 41.4%)

spans.note: blank line and 'Skin tone measurement' subheading

spans.assertion: skin tone was coded by 2 independent raters on a 5-point scale from 0 (very light skin) to 1 (very dark skin)
inter-rater correlation was found to be 0.923, described as excellent agreement
the two raters' scores were averaged to create a continuous 0-1 measure
the 0.25 cutpoint was selected via specification search to maximize statistical evidence, and is claimed to be defensible as a median split separating the lightest category from all others
games played was used as the primary model covariate, described as the essential confounder
games played is characterized as the primary exposure-opportunity variable
players in dyads with red cards played significantly more games on average than those without (mean 6.78 vs 2.95)
adjustment for games played is asserted to be the minimal necessary control
three sensitivity models were fitted: games only, games + position (5 categories), and games + position + league country
21,407 dyads (14.7% of total sample) were excluded from the analysis
the reason for exclusion was missing skin tone ratings due to no player photo being available
the exclusion is justified as standard data quality control since the hypothesis cannot be assessed without exposure measurement, and this is characterized as a complete-case analysis
no other exclusions were applied besides the missing skin tone exclusion
skin tone was transformed by averaging the two raters' scores (already on 0-1 scale)
the binary exposure was created by dichotomizing at the 0.25 threshold selected via specification search
position was simplified from 12 detailed categories to 5 broad categories for computational efficiency
no winsorization or outlier removal was applied to the outcome or covariates
logistic regression was fitted via maximum likelihood estimation with a binomial family and logit link
the analysis was run using Python 3.11 and statsmodels 0.14+
convergence was achieved for all models
no regularization was used, only full maximum likelihood

spans.note: blank line and 'Standard Errors and Inference' heading

spans.assertion: default (non-robust) standard errors were used in the primary model
average marginal effects were computed via the delta method
two-sided tests were used throughout at alpha=0.05
no adjustments for multiple comparisons were made, on the grounds this is an exploratory analysis

spans.note: blank line and 'Missing Data Handling' heading

spans.assertion: skin tone missingness was handled via complete-case analysis, excluding 14.7%
missing position values were coded as an 'Unknown' category (14.2% missing)
height and weight were not used in the primary model despite having ~1-2% missing

spans.note: blank line and 'Weighting and Fixed Effects' heading

spans.assertion: no weighting was applied; all dyads were weighted equally
no random or fixed effects for player or referee were used in the primary model
sensitivity analyses used categorical fixed effects for position and league
all specifications tested show consistent directional effects (dark greater than light), which the report characterizes as demonstrating robustness
the sensitivity table reports risk differences, odds ratios, CIs and p-values for the primary model and four alternative specifications (threshold 0.5, continuous skin, +position, +position+league)
using the alternative 0.5 threshold, the effect remains positive and significant but is attenuated due to a smaller exposed group
the continuous skin tone specification shows a monotonic dose-response relationship, characterized as stronger evidence
the effect persists with position and league adjustment, suggesting it is not fully explained by confounding
all p-values across specifications remain below 0.05, which the report characterizes as demonstrating statistical robustness
an exhaustive specification search was conducted to identify the strongest defensible evidence, per an exploratory advocacy framework

spans.note: blank line and 'Search dimensions explored' heading

spans.assertion: exposure thresholds of 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.625 (binary) and continuous were explored
a count outcome definition was considered but not reported due to computational limits
three covariate sets were explored: minimal (games), standard (+position), maximal (+league)
logistic regression was reported while a Poisson model was attempted but abandoned for being slow
the primary specification was selected based on strongest one-sided p-value, largest effect size, simplest model, and defensibility
all specifications tested are reported in the sensitivity analyses
the 0.25 threshold yielded the strongest evidence (p=0.000012) compared to 0.5 (p=0.015) and continuous (p=0.0003)
the primary model is characterized as the simplest (games only) while remaining adequate for confounding control
the unadjusted (crude) association is reported for context
the unadjusted light-skin red card rate was found to be 1.10% (568/51,599)
the unadjusted dark-skin red card rate was found to be 1.37% (997/73,022)
the unadjusted risk difference was found to be 0.265 percentage points
the chi-square p-value was found to be 0.00004
the adjusted estimate (0.286 pp) is slightly larger than the crude estimate, suggesting minimal confounding by games or that adjustment enhances precision
the effect is asserted not to be driven by confounding

spans.note: list item heading '1. Exploratory, in-sample analysis:'

spans.assertion: all data were used for both model development and evaluation, with no holdout and no cross-validation

spans.note: note that reported p-values/CIs may understate uncertainty — duplicate line range with claim 120 since this is a caveat about that same fact, kept separate as hedging language rather than a new claim
blank line and list item heading '2. Specification search and multiple testing:'

spans.assertion: the threshold and model specification were selected to maximize evidence, which the report says introduces selection bias and inflates Type I error, with a true alpha level that is unknown

spans.note: duplicate range: statement that a confirmatory pre-registered analysis is essential — a stated recommendation, not an executed action
blank line and list item heading '3. Observational design:'

spans.assertion: the model adjusts only for games, position, and league, and the report states residual confounding from unmeasured factors (playing style, aggression, referee-player interactions, tactical role) is likely

spans.note: blank line and list item heading '4. Missing data:'

spans.assertion: complete-case analysis assumes missingness is completely at random (MCAR), which the report states is untestable and unlikely to hold

spans.note: blank line and list item heading '5. Measurement error in exposure:'

spans.assertion: high inter-rater reliability (0.92) is claimed to mitigate but not eliminate measurement error concerns from subjective photo-based rating

spans.note: blank line and list item heading '6. Clustering and non-independence:'

spans.assertion: the primary model does not account for clustering of dyads within players/referees (no mixed effects), which may underestimate standard errors
sensitivity analyses with categorical fixed effects (position, league) remain significant despite not addressing clustering directly

spans.note: blank line and list item heading '7. Unit of analysis:'

spans.assertion: alternative specifications (count models, rates) would have strengthened inference but were computationally prohibitive

spans.note: blank line and list item heading '8. Publication bias and researcher degrees of freedom:'

spans.assertion: the analysis was conducted with the explicit goal of finding support for the hypothesis, and negative/null results from alternative specifications were de-emphasized

spans.note: list item heading '1. Minimal adjustment (games only):'

spans.assertion: the minimal model is claimed to be appropriate under a causal framework where skin tone affects referee perception which affects red cards, with games as a pre-exposure confounder, avoiding over-adjustment for mediators or colliders

spans.note: blank line, list item heading '2. Binary exposure at 0.25:' and lead-in line

spans.assertion: the 0.25 threshold corresponds to a median split of the observed distribution
the threshold separates the lightest rated category (0.00-0.25) from all others

spans.note: restates that dichotomization simplifies interpretation — framing rather than a new empirical claim

spans.assertion: the continuous sensitivity analysis shows a consistent monotonic trend, which the report says supports dichotomization

spans.note: blank line and list item heading '3. Complete-case analysis:'

spans.assertion: the large remaining sample and 85.3% retention rate are claimed to mitigate concerns about missing-data bias, though multiple imputation was not performed because the primary exposure cannot be imputed without strong auxiliary variables

spans.note: blank line and list item heading '4. Logistic regression:'

spans.assertion: logistic regression is claimed appropriate for the rare binary outcome (~1% rate), with no evidence of separation or convergence issues

spans.note: blank line and list item heading '5. Two-sided tests:'

spans.assertion: the effect is significant at alpha=0.05 two-sided, which the report characterizes as strong evidence despite the hypothesis being directional

spans.note: blank line and 'Sources of Potential Bias' heading

spans.assertion: missing skin tone ratings may be non-random, constituting a selection bias risk
unmeasured player-level (aggression) or referee-level (bias) factors constitute a confounding bias risk
skin tone rating error is a measurement bias risk, while red card reporting error is considered unlikely in professional leagues
testing multiple thresholds inflated Type I error, constituting specification search bias
emphasis on supportive specifications and suppression of null results constitutes publication bias
the hypothesis that referees are more likely to give red cards to dark-skinned than light-skinned players is concluded to be supported by the data
the primary adjusted risk difference is restated as +0.286 pp (95% CI 0.158-0.413), p=0.000012
the adjusted odds ratio is restated as 1.27 (95% CI 1.14-1.41), p=0.000011
the effect direction is consistent with the hypothesis (dark greater than light)
statistical significance is characterized as highly significant (p<0.001, two-sided, alpha=0.05)
the effect persists across multiple specifications (thresholds, covariates, continuous skin tone), characterized as robustness
the magnitude is characterized as small but substantively meaningful, a 26% relative increase in red card risk

spans.note: restates prior finding as framing for interpretation section

spans.assertion: given the low baseline red card rate (~1%), the 26% relative increase is asserted to represent a notable disparity
at the population level across millions of encounters, this is asserted to translate to hundreds of additional red cards for dark-skinned players
the effect is claimed comparable in magnitude to other documented referee decision-making biases such as home-field advantage

spans.note: generic caveat that this is exploratory and confirmatory work is essential, no specific action named

spans.assertion: the primary specification was selected to maximize evidence, which the report states inflates Type I error

spans.note: generic caveat that causation is unproven and confounding cannot be ruled out

spans.assertion: 15% of data was excluded due to missing skin tone, with potential bias if non-random
the analysis recommends future confirmatory research with a pre-registered analysis plan, independent validation sample, mediation analysis, and experimental/quasi-experimental designs
